name: libffi
notes: CURRENT Windows verification (2026-08-25), superseding all later historical notes that still describe a repeat-call defect or partial status: the corrected common test matrix passes call-static, call-shared, repeat-call-static -O1, and repeat-call-shared -O1 against the CRT-built libffi.a and libffi.dll.a. Together with the real Linux and macOS results above, libffi is shared-pass on all three hosts.

CURRENT Linux aarch64 verification (2026-08-25), superseding all later historical notes that still describe Linux as partial: the corrected common test matrix passes call-static, call-shared, repeat-call-static -O1, and repeat-call-shared -O1 against the CRT-built libffi.a and libffi.so. Linux keeps its native target macros consistently between the library and consumers, so it never needed the Darwin generated-header adaptation; the register-sized ffi_arg return buffer correction applies normally. Linux is shared-pass.

RESOLVED macOS arm64 optimized repeat-call failure (2026-08-25), superseding every older X19/callee-saved-register diagnosis later in this historical notes array: there was no demonstrated libffi assembly register-corruption defect. Two consumer-side ABI violations combined to produce the optimization-dependent SIGSEGV. First, both committed ffi_call tests passed a 4-byte int as rvalue even though libffi's documented ffi_call contract requires register-sized storage and its aarch64 return path writes a full ffi_arg; both tests now use ffi_arg. Second, the library build used -D__APPLE__=1 while normal crt-cc consumers intentionally see -U__APPLE__. libffi's generated ffitarget.h therefore gave the library a Darwin-only aarch64_nfixedargs field in ffi_cif but omitted it from the consumer's ffi_cif. ffi_prep_cif wrote that hidden field over the following values[0] pointer; the crash report caught ffi_call_int/memcpy reading the resulting 0x100000000 address. A target-scoped post_install_patch now changes the installed generated header to select the same field for CRT_TARGET_OS_MACOS, preserving the Bionic-shaped compiler surface without leaking __APPLE__ to general consumers or patching upstream source. A fresh port-rebuild-libffi plus port-test-libffi passes call-static, call-shared, repeat-call-static -O1, and repeat-call-shared -O1 on real macOS arm64, so macOS is shared-pass. Linux does not hide __linux__ and Windows keeps _WIN32 consistently, so this specific layout mismatch is Darwin-only; the corrected ffi_arg tests apply consistently across all three hosts, whose current results are recorded immediately above.

windows aarch64: the repeat-call register-corruption bug (`repeat-call-static`/`repeat-call-shared` in this recipe's own `tests` array) DID NOT REPRODUCE in a fresh, from-clean rebuild on this project's aarch64 Windows dev machine -- 20/20 clean passes at -O1 (the committed test's own flag) and 10/10 at -O2 (tried separately, matching the documented "reproduces at both -O1/-O2" characterization), full recipe test suite green, full ctest 88/88. This directly contradicts the most recent prior finding (2026-08-15, same machine, same test) that it reproduces reliably. No change was made to libffi's own source, build flags, FFI_DEFAULT_ABI override, or anything in sysv.S/ffi.c during this session -- the only unrelated change landed in between was a Windows PAL fix for a separate make -jN hang (see TODO.md/HISTORY.md, __crt_sys_fstat()/windows_handle_looks_executable()), which shares no code path with libffi's own aarch64 calling-convention assembly. Not declaring this fixed: the cause of the non-reproduction itself is unknown (possibly a host LLVM/toolchain update between 2026-08-15 and now, possibly the bug was always narrower/more timing-sensitive than the earlier 100%-reproducing characterization suggested -- neither confirmed). Status stays `partial` pending either a repeated failure to restore confidence this is still a real, live bug worth the planned `lldb` single-step investigation, or enough clean runs across enough rebuilds to reconsider it. `lldb` itself is now actually usable on this machine (previously blocked on a missing python311.dll -- installing Python 3.11 and putting it on PATH fixes this) for whenever a reproducible failure shows up again to debug against.

windows: shared-library build achieved and verified end-to-end (x86_64), superseding the 'shared attempted... build_libtool_libs resolves to no' entry below -- three more real, independent bugs found and fixed, all general/root-caused, none upstream-source patches:

1. The exact same libtool/ld.lld auto-import misdetection documented in libpng.json's own notes and fixed generically in tools/crt-native-tool (inject the right `ld.lld -m i386pep`/`-m arm64pe` emulation so a bare `$LD --help` probe sees the same real, capable personality tools/crt-cc's own compiler-driven links already use) -- already-generic fix, simply applies here unmodified once libpng's fix landed.

2. A severe, general Windows fork() correctness bug in libc/src/malloc.c (unrelated to libtool/libffi specifically, but found while chasing an apparent 'hang' rebuilding this port): the OS-region tracking table fork_memcopy.c relies on silently stopped recording new heap regions past 256MB, so a long-lived, memory-growing process (a deeply self-recursive `mksh` interpreting libffi's own large `libtool` script) could fork() into a child running on silently-missing memory -- indistinguishable from a hang or an intermittent crash. Fixed generally (raised the cap to 4GB, and turned any future overflow into an honest allocation failure instead of silent corruption) -- see libc/src/malloc.c's own comment and TODO.md's dedicated entry for the full writeup and repro.

3. The real, final blocker, specific to this port: libffi's own Makefile.am unconditionally sets `AM_LTLDFLAGS = -no-undefined -bindir "$(bindir)"` for every host. GNU Libtool's `func_relative_path`/`func_normal_abspath` (called only when both `-bindir` and a real shared build coincide -- confirmed by bisecting each flag independently) determine 'is this path absolute' by checking for a literal leading `/`; a genuine Windows drive-letter absolute path (`C:/Users/...`) never matches, so it's treated as relative, `pwd` (itself also a non-'/'-prefixed Windows path in this environment) gets prepended, and the resulting string never starts with `/` either -- every subsequent sed-based path-component step in the same function also requires a leading `/` to make any progress, so the ascend-to-root loop never terminates: an unconditional, unbounded loop forking a fresh `echo`/`sed` pair every iteration, confirmed directly by extracting and single-stepping `func_dirname`/`func_normal_abspath` in isolation. Since this lives inside libtool's own generated script (not reachable via a recipe CFLAGS override, and not something to hand-patch a regenerated-every-run file), fixed via the sanctioned, standard mechanism `AM_LTLDFLAGS` is a real Automake convention: override it from `make`'s own command line to drop just the offending `-bindir` while keeping the legitimate `-no-undefined` requirement. Needed *two* mechanisms together, not one: a plain command-line `VAR=value` override (a new, general `target_overrides.<os>.make_args` recipe field, merged the same way `configure_args`/`cflags` already are) reaches the *first* `make` invocation correctly, but libffi's own `SUBDIRS = include testsuite man doc .` causes a *recursive* self-invocation of the same Makefile to actually build `libffi.la` -- and that recursive submake was NOT correctly inheriting the command-line override (root cause not fully isolated: plausibly this project's own Windows process-spawn implementation not perfectly preserving GNU Make's own MAKEFLAGS-based recursive-variable-propagation convention). Sidestepped by also exporting `AM_LTLDFLAGS` as a real environment variable and adding `-e` (`--environment-overrides`) to make_args, which relies on ordinary OS-level environment inheritance across process spawns instead -- a much more fundamental mechanism the whole build already depends on working correctly, and confirmed robust across the actual recursive build (not just a `-n` dry run).

Verified end-to-end on Windows x86_64: `libffi-8.dll` + `libffi.dll.a` build and install cleanly (make: 85.5s, make install: 18.7s, no hangs), and a standalone test program dynamically loaded the real DLL via dlopen()/dlsym() and ran a genuine ffi_call() round trip (add_ints(3, 4) == 7) through it. Full ctest 79/79 throughout every step of this chain. Not re-verified on aarch64 this session (all three fixes are architecture-generic, so should apply equally, but aarch64 specifically wasn't re-run) -- and the pre-existing, KNOWN, aarch64-specific X19 double-call bug documented below is completely unrelated to shared-vs-static linking and was not re-tested for a possible x86_64 analogue (only a single ffi_call() was exercised this session, not the two-calls-in-a-row repro that trips X19 on aarch64) -- status stays 'partial' rather than 'shared-pass' for that reason: the shared-library *build* capability is now solid, but the family of known-and-possibly-unknown ffi_call()-repeat-call correctness issues is untouched.
Upstream provides a normal Autoconf configure flow, so build.system records configure rather than manual.
macOS/aarch64 upstream libffi uses its Darwin trampoline-table path; any required compatibility must be provided by the CRT sysroot/PAL, not by patching libffi sources.

target_overrides.macos.env forces gcc_cv_as_cfi_pseudo_op=no because libffi's simple configure probe succeeds while its real Darwin aarch64 CFI assembly does not assemble through the CRT wrapper. Scoped to macOS since the note is specifically about Darwin aarch64 assembly; Linux/Windows have not shown the same probe/reality mismatch (status: partial on both, not yet root-caused either way), so this is not assumed to also apply there.
macOS/aarch64 ffi_call and ffi_closure_alloc/ffi_prep_closure_loc smoke tests passed against the installed static libffi.

Windows: config.guess doesn't recognize plain Windows uname output, same as libpng/zlib -- worked around with --build=@CRT_MINGW_TRIPLE@, resolved by tools/crt-port-build.py's own arch detection (--target-arch flag, else CRT_TARGET_ARCH env var, else platform.machine()) to aarch64-w64-mingw32 or x86_64-w64-mingw32, so this works unmodified on either Windows architecture (only aarch64 has actually been exercised so far, being the only Windows arch this dev machine can run natively).

Windows: libffi's own build system generates a broken top-level 'multilib dispatcher' Makefile (piped through a bundled sed script -- makefile.sed -- that assumes Unix paths and mishandles a Windows drive-letter colon as a Makefile target separator, corrupting substituted values like MAKE=C:/...). target_overrides.windows.make_subdir (@CRT_MINGW_TRIPLE@, same substitution as --build= above) routes make/make install straight at the real, uncorrupted Makefile in that subdirectory instead (see tools/crt-port-build.py's own comment on build_configure_port's make_subdir handling).

Windows aarch64: dlmalloc.c (vendored into src/closures.c) and src/aarch64/ffi.c both #include <windows.h> when _WIN32 is defined (VirtualAlloc-family memory management for closures/mmap, and FlushInstructionCache) -- this project's sysroot has no real Windows SDK <windows.h> (its own Win32 API surface is declared privately inside libc/src/arch/windows/, not exposed publicly). Tried undefining _WIN32/WIN32 (the same -U CFLAGS technique zlib/libpng/sqlite-amalgamation use) to route these files onto their generic POSIX mmap()/mprotect() path instead, since this project's own libc genuinely implements both -- but reverted it after discovering _WIN32 also gates several *other*, unrelated decisions in libffi's own aarch64 port: src/aarch64/ffitarget.h disables FFI_GO_CLOSURES specifically because Windows reserves the X18 register for the TEB pointer (`/* iOS and Windows reserve x18 for the system. Disable Go closures until a new static chain is chosen. */`) -- undefining _WIN32 silently re-enabled that code path, corrupting X18 on every single ffi_call(), not just Go-closures ones (caught via a real, reproducible segfault, root-caused with a disassembly check confirming the X18-clobbering instruction and a VectoredExceptionHandler-based crash probe). It also changes FFI_DEFAULT_ABI (FFI_WIN64 -> FFI_SYSV), which would then differ from what any real consumer compiling against the installed ffi.h normally (no special -U flags) would see, since ffi_abi's default is resolved at the *consumer's* compile time, not baked into the library. Undoing just the X18 issue via a source patch (restoring FFI_GO_CLOSURES's guard using this project's own always-on CRT_TARGET_OS_WINDOWS marker instead of the _WIN32 our CFLAGS removes) was tried and technically worked, but left the FFI_DEFAULT_ABI mismatch unaddressed and required patching upstream source for a problem this project's own CFLAGS choice created in the first place.

Windows aarch64: settled on providing porting/shims/win32/windows.h instead -- a small, project-owned header (same __declspec(dllimport) declaration style already used throughout libc/src/arch/windows/, field-for-field verified against a real Windows SDK winnt.h/sysinfoapi.h) covering exactly the APIs dlmalloc.c/ffi.c call (VirtualAlloc/VirtualFree/VirtualQuery, GetSystemInfo, FlushInstructionCache, Sleep). target_overrides.windows.include_dirs (a new, general recipe mechanism -- see tools/crt-port-build.py's apply_recipe_env) adds it to CPPFLAGS. This keeps _WIN32 defined normally throughout the whole build, so every one of libffi's own Windows-aware decisions (X18/Go-closures avoidance, FFI_WIN64 default ABI, FFI_MMAP_EXEC_WRIT) resolves exactly as upstream intends and exactly as a real downstream consumer of the installed library will also see it, with zero upstream source patches.

Windows aarch64: InterlockedCompareExchange, InterlockedExchange, and InterlockedCompareExchangePointer (all called by dlmalloc.c's Win32 spinlock path) turned out to NOT be real kernel32 DLL exports at all -- real winnt.h defines all three as compiler intrinsics (#pragma intrinsic), confirmed the hard way via a real 'undefined symbol: __declspec(dllimport) InterlockedCompareExchange' link error after declaring them that way. porting/shims/win32/windows.h implements all three via real Clang/GCC __sync_* builtins instead (__sync_val_compare_and_swap, __sync_lock_test_and_set), each paired with a #define of the same name (InterlockedCompareExchangePointer in particular is only reached by dlmalloc.c's own #ifdef InterlockedCompareExchangePointer check, which tests for a macro, not a same-named function -- a function-only first attempt silently fell through to the wrong, 32-bit-truncating branch).

Windows aarch64: __clear_cache() (libc/src/arch/windows/common/compiler_abi.c) was also needed -- a standard GCC/Clang builtin-runtime symbol this project's Windows builds had no compiler-rt builtins archive to provide at all (clang's own --print-libgcc-file-name comes up empty for this LLVM install/target). Implemented via the real Win32 FlushInstructionCache() API.

SUPERSEDED by the shared-library success recorded at the top of this notes array -- kept as the historical trail of the original investigation. Windows: shared attempted (removed --disable-shared/--enable-static from configure_args, matching zlib/libpng's convention of leaving libtool's own default alone rather than forcing static) and confirmed to hit the exact same GNU-Libtool/lld-link mismatch documented in porting/recipes/libpng.json's notes -- build_libtool_libs resolves to no, so the build silently falls back to installing only libffi.a, exactly as before. tools/crt-port-build.py's make_env() was subsequently extended (while investigating libpng) to pre-set $DLLTOOL/$OBJDUMP to llvm-dlltool/llvm-objdump, which fixed those two probes but did not flip build_libtool_libs to yes -- see libpng.json's notes for the full root-cause writeup and what's still unresolved; it applies unmodified here since both ports go through the same Autoconf+Libtool machinery. The pre-existing 'partial' status below (the X19-corruption bug) is unrelated to shared-vs-static and unaffected either way.

Linux/macOS: unlike Windows, this port's own shared library actually builds successfully on both hosts via real GNU Libtool + system ld/ld64 -- discovered while chasing zlib's Linux-only shared-link bug (see zlib.json's own notes): 'libffi/libpng shared builds succeeded [on a real Linux aarch64 host]' even before that fix landed, since neither port happened to pull in the specific libc.a stdio.c.o symbol that tripped zlib's failure. This is independent of, and unrelated to, the X19 runtime bug documented below, which is a pure ffi_call() correctness issue, not a link/build problem -- status stays partial on Linux for that reason regardless.

Windows aarch64, KNOWN UNRESOLVED ISSUE (why status stays 'partial', matching Linux): the full build succeeds and installs cleanly, and ffi_call() alone and ffi_closure_alloc()/ffi_prep_closure_loc() alone (a real trampoline, exercising the VirtualAlloc/mprotect-equivalent PROT_EXEC path) each smoke-test successfully in isolation -- but calling ffi_call() and THEN making any further libffi call in the same process (a second ffi_prep_cif(), or ffi_closure_alloc()/ffi_prep_closure_loc(), it doesn't matter which) reliably segfaults, IF the caller was compiled at -O1 or -O2 (never reproduces at -O0). Root-caused down to: disassembly of a minimal ~20-line repro (ffi_prep_cif -> ffi_call -> ffi_prep_cif again, zero closures involved) shows clang -O1/-O2 caching a live value (e.g. the arg_types pointer) in a callee-saved GPR (X19 in the observed case) across the ffi_call() call, trusting AAPCS64's callee-saved-register guarantee -- and something in the ffi_call()/ffi_call_SYSV call chain (src/aarch64/ffi.c + the hand-written src/aarch64/sysv.S, which uses an unusual 'mov sp, x0' caller-provided-stack-frame convention rather than a normal prologue) does not preserve it, so the second call receives a corrupted argument and crashes dereferencing it. Ruled out during investigation: X18/TEB corruption (confirmed clean via disassembly -- no x18 in the built library at all), instruction-cache staleness (a manual, definitely-correct __builtin___clear_cache() call from outside libffi, redundant with the library's own internal flush, made no difference), and shared/reused ffi_cif state (crashes identically with two entirely separate ffi_cif objects). Given libffi's aarch64 assembly is extremely widely used at -O2 on Linux/macOS without this kind of report, this is suspected to be specific to some interaction between sysv.S's stack-repointing trick and either this project's own crt-cc-generated prologue/frame layout or the aarch64-w64-mingw32 target's ABI details -- not yet narrowed further; would need single-stepping ffi_call()'s own compiled code (not just the hand-written assembly) with a real debugger to pin down exactly where X19 stops being preserved. Real, minimal repro kept for whoever picks this back up (was in scratch_verify/ffi_diag7.c during the investigating session, not committed -- recreate from this note if needed: prep_cif, ffi_call(add_ints), prep_cif again, no closures, compiled at -O1).

**Historical x86_64 Windows result: the callee-saved-register regression is clean there, but the former conclusion that the bug was aarch64-Windows-specific is superseded by the 2026-08-25 macOS arm64 reproduction at the top of this notes array.** The exact documented repro (`ffi_prep_cif` -> `ffi_call(add_ints)` -> `ffi_prep_cif` again, no closures) was never actually preserved as a committed test -- it only ever lived in an uncommitted scratch file on the aarch64 session that found it. Recreated it as a permanent regression, `porting/tests/libffi_repeat_call_test.c`, wired into this recipe's own `tests` array as `repeat-call-static`/`repeat-call-shared`, cflags forcing `-O1` explicitly (the documented trigger level). On a real x86_64 Windows host: passes cleanly at both `-O1` and `-O2` (temporarily tried both; committed test stays at `-O1`, the documented minimal trigger), both static and shared, repeatably. Also independently established (reading `ffi.c`/`Makefile.am`) that `win64_armasm.S` (MSVC ARMASM syntax) and `sysv.S` (GNU/LLVM syntax) implement the identical symbol set for two different assemblers, not two different ABI code paths -- this project's clang+LLVM-integrated-assembler toolchain always uses `sysv.S` regardless of `FFI_SYSV`/`FFI_WIN64` `cif->abi` selection, and `ffi.c` calls `ffi_call_SYSV` unconditionally either way (`abi` only changes behavior for variadics/HFA floats, neither of which `add_ints(int,int)` exercises) -- so this recipe's earlier `FFI_DEFAULT_ABI` override (`FFI_WIN64` -> `FFI_SYSV`, added for an unrelated X18/TEB reason, see the Go-closures note above) is very unlikely to be the actual cause of the register-corruption bug. Next step: isolate the exact arm64 instruction/state transition on a host where the committed regression reproduces; macOS arm64 is now a reliable local repro, while Linux arm64 still needs the current matrix rerun.
